newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-NO SLIP-UP FOR GERMANY AS WORLD CUP DESCENDS INTO FARCE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NO SLIP-UP FOR GERMANY AS WORLD CUP DESCENDS INTO FARCE.

text.p: Ruthless German efficiency and utter Estonian farce emphasised the huge gulf in class between the best and the worst soccer nations in Europe on Wednesday.

While injury-hit European champions Germany, without seven key players, brushed Armenia aside 5-1 in a group nine qualifier in Yerevan, Estonia failed even to turn up for their group four match against Scotland in Tallinn.

The farce in Tallinn arose because Scotland, with FIFA's backing, asked for the kick-off time to be brought forward nearly three hours because of the poor standard of temporary floodlighting in the stadium.

Although the kick-off was agreed in advance between all the necessary officials, the Estonian team failed to turn up for the match which lasted for three seconds. The Estonians claimed they could not get from their training ground to the stadium in time.
Scotland could and kicked off to get the match technically underway before Yugoslav referee Miroslav Radoman stopped it almost immediately.
FIFA will rule on the incident on November 7 and are virtually certain to award Scotland a 3-0 victory.
While the points from that non-event are yet to be awarded, there was another surprise in the same group later on Wednesday when Austria beat Sweden 1-0 in Stockholm.
The only goal came after 11 minutes through Andreas Herzog to dent Sweden's 100 percent record and lift Austria -- temporarily at least -- level on points with Scotland after two games.
There was another notable result in Tel Aviv where Israel held Russia to a 1-1 draw in group five thanks to a Gadi Brumer goal for the home side after 64 minutes.
Igor Kolyvanov equalised for Russia 11 minutes from time which leaves those two teams top of the group with four points from two matches. Russia lead the standings on goal difference.

Germany, playing their first match in this campaign and without seven regulars, do not lead group nine yet but showed they have lost none of their power in their emphatic 5-1 victory over minnows Armenia.

Thomas Haessler (20th and 39th minutes), skipper Juergen Klinsmann (26th), Fredi Bobic (69th) and Stefan Kuntz (80th) all scored for the Germans before Karapet Mikaelyan scored a consolation for the home side just before the end.
Ukraine stay top of the group but Portugal improved their standing to second with a 3-0 win in Albania.
Denmark joined Greece level on points at the top of group one after beating the Greeks 2-1 in Copenhagen.

A Theodoros Zagorakis own goal after 25 minutes gave Denmark the lead before Georgios Donis equalised after 35 minutes. Brian Laudrup secured the points for the home side five minutes after half-time.
Kjetil Rekdal scored a hat-trick in the last seven minutes of a group three match in Oslo to give Norway a 3-0 win over Hungary.
